hints: Use the power formula $P = F_D \times v$ with power $160\text{ W}$ and speed $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to find the driving force $F_D = 32\text{ N}$.
Apply Newton's second law on the horizontal road: $F_D - F_{\text{res}} = ma$.
Substitute $F_{\text{res}} = 20\text{ N}$ and acceleration $a = 0.15\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to show that total mass is $80\text{ kg}$.
walkthrough:
First, calculate the forward driving force $F_D$ developed by the cyclist when working at $160\text{ W}$ at speed $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = F_D v \implies F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{160}{5} = 32\text{ N}$$

Next, apply Newton's second law ($F_{\text{net}} = ma$) along the level road. The forward driving force is opposed by the constant resistance force of $20\text{ N}$:
$$F_{\text{net}} = F_D - F_{\text{res}} = 32 - 20 = 12\text{ N}$$

Equate net force to mass times acceleration ($a = 0.15\text{ m s}^{-2}$):
$$12 = ma = m(0.15)$$
$$m = \frac{12}{0.15} = \frac{1200}{15} = 80\text{ kg}$$

hints: At steady speed up the $2^\circ$ hill, acceleration is zero, so the driving force balances both the resistance ($20\text{ N}$) and the downhill component of weight ($mg\sin 2^\circ$).
Use $P = F_D \times v$ with power $300\text{ W}$ to solve for the steady speed $v$.
walkthrough:
When traveling at a steady speed up an incline, acceleration is zero ($a = 0$). By Newton's first law, the upward driving force $F_D$ must balance resistance plus the component of weight down the slope:
$$F_D = F_{\text{res}} + mg\sin\theta$$

Substitute mass $m = 80\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, angle $\theta = 2^\circ$, and resistance $20\text{ N}$:
$$F_D = 20 + 80 \times 10 \times \sin 2^\circ = 20 + 800\sin 2^\circ$$
$$F_D = 20 + 800(0.034899) = 20 + 27.9196 = 47.9196\text{ N}$$

The cyclist works at power $P = 300\text{ W}$. Use $P = F_D \times v$:
$$300 = 47.9196 v$$
$$v = \frac{300}{47.9196} \approx 6.2605\text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 6.26\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

hints: Calculate 90% of the steady speed: $v = 0.9 \times 6.26\text{ m s}^{-1} = 5.634\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Calculate the new driving force at this speed from power $300\text{ W}$: $F_D = \frac{300}{5.634} \approx 53.25\text{ N}$.
Apply Newton's second law up the slope: $F_D - (20 + 800\sin 2^\circ) = ma$, and solve for acceleration $a$.
walkthrough:
The cyclist travels at $90\%$ of the steady speed found in part (ii):
$$v = 0.90 \times 6.2605 = 5.6345\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Working at the same power of $300\text{ W}$, the driving force at this lower speed is:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{300}{5.6345} \approx 53.2434\text{ N}$$
The opposing forces remain constant: resistance of $20\text{ N}$ plus weight component $800\sin 2^\circ = 27.9196\text{ N}$, giving a total opposing force of $47.9196\text{ N}$.

Apply Newton's second law ($F_{\text{net}} = ma$) up the incline:
$$F_D - F_{\text{opposing}} = ma$$
$$53.2434 - 47.9196 = 80a$$
$$5.3238 = 80a$$

Divide both sides by $80$ to find the acceleration:
$$a = \frac{5.3238}{80} \approx 0.06655\text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 0.0666\text{ m s}^{-2}\text{ up the hill}$$
